messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for streaming inference in eu-west-1. Auto-paging oncall.

rachel_oncall: taking lead. Datadog shows p95 ~ 350ms -> 1.1s and p99 hitting ~2.9s in the last 15m. Users report streaming stalls and partial responses. Opening thread to triage.

jess_runtime: seeing token emission stalls in haproxy and our stream muxer. Some streams pause for 8-30s then emit bursts. Affected pools: euw-stream-01/02. Links: https://datadog.redwood/streaming/eu-west-1?from=now-30m

tara_net: network telemetry indicates elevated retransmits and increased RTT on inter-AZ fabric between eu-west-1a <-> eu-west-1b. Transit gateway attachments show packet drop spikes. Also seeing TLS handshake tail increase from 80ms -> 1.1s at our front proxies.

mike_sre: can we confirm if TLS resumption is failing? If so, handshake cost could explain some of the tail.

jess_runtime: checking proxy stats... resumption rate dropped ~50% for the affected time window. Might be connection churn + packet loss causing resumption failures. Also haproxy reports lots of 'client-timed-out' between accept and first write.

ops-bot: Suggested mitigations: (A) prefer AZ-local NAT/egress within VPC for affected subnets (fast, reversible). (B) enable local fallback routing for streaming hostpool. (C) widen keepalive and increase TLS session cache as temporary config tweaks.

rachel_oncall: let's go with A first — low blast radius. Jess, can you run a canary by switching one streaming subnet to AZ-local egress? Post the exact command you use.

jess_runtime: will run canary on subnet-stream-a. Command:
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-subnet-stream-a --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --network-interface-id eni-nat-local-eu1a
```
Applying now, monitoring p95/p99 for flows sourced from that subnet.

deploy-bot: route change requested for rtb-subnet-stream-a queued -> applied.

tara_net: capturing packet trace on the problematic path, uploading pcap now to incident bucket.

jess_runtime: canary applied. Observed immediate improvement: p99 for that subnet fell from 2.6s -> 280ms within 70s. Nice signal that cross-AZ egress path was contributing.

mike_sre: roll to remaining streaming subnets in the region. Also increase TLS session cache on proxies and enable session tickets to improve resumption.

jess_runtime: rolling to subnet-stream-b and subnet-stream-c now.

ops-bot: change applied to rtb-subnet-stream-b; change applied to rtb-subnet-stream-c.

tara_net: provider-side telemetry shows packet drops on transit peer between zone a and b matching the incident window. Opening provider ticket and attaching tcpdump and retransmit graphs.

mike_sre: customer impact note: create short message for status page. Leo, can you draft? We should mention partial degradation, mitigation applied, and we're investigating with provider.

leo_prod: drafted: "We detected elevated streaming latency in eu-west-1 affecting some inference requests. We've applied routing mitigations which have reduced impact. We're coordinating with our transit provider and will update in 60 minutes." Will publish after review.

sam_support: pushing update to affected customers (orgs: gamma-ai, delta-ops, epsilon-ml). Notifying them of mitigation and suggested client-side backoff/retry for streaming stalls.

jess_runtime: saving artifacts for postmortem: haproxy_stream_stalls.log, dd-trace-bad-streams.json, tcpdump-euw-14_52.pcap, datadog_screens/streaming-spike-14_50.png. Uploading to incident case.

mike_sre: next steps: 1) keep AZ-local egress in place for 2 hours to confirm stability; 2) escalate with provider for root cause and timeline; 3) collect TLS histograms and connection churn metrics for postmortem; 4) schedule incident review tomorrow.

rachel_oncall: I'll handoff to mike_sre in 30m. Current snapshot at handoff time: p95 340ms, p99 420ms, client error rate slightly elevated but trending down. Mitigation in place: AZ-local egress + TLS session cache tune. Provider engaged.

mike_sre: acknowledged, taking over. I'll maintain routing changes and coordinate with provider. If we see recurrence, plan B is to expand local NAT capacity and consider regional fallback endpoints.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations executed, provider engaged. Participants: rachel_oncall, mike_sre, jess_runtime, tara_net, sam_support, leo_prod. Incident is active. Last update 1763022380."
